name: Chainsaw

comps.spec: Saw chain, guide bar and drive sprocket; spare chains are often in a drawer nearby
Bar and chain oil, 0.14–0.28 L in the tank on the saws checked (Oregon CS1500, Husqvarna 450 II, STIHL MS 162/172); often a jug nearby

notes: Pick a variant: petrol or electric. Whole working saws get taken; spare chains and bars are often left behind. A spare chain fits only if its pitch matches the drive sprocket (and the bar's nose sprocket, if it has one), its gauge fits the bar groove and its drive-link count suits the bar (STIHL MS 162/172, Oregon M&S 2004). Chainsaws are loud: CCOHS puts them at up to 95–115 dBA, so wear muffs or plugs (CCOHS chainsaw PPE).

sources.title: Oregon M&S 2004: Oregon (Blount), Maintenance & Safety Manual for Saw Chain, Guide Bars, and Drive Sprockets (F/N A106971 AG 0904), Oregon's own PDF, pp. 4-5 (chain terms), 21 (oil), 88-91 (sprockets) and 95 (ordering chain)
STIHL MS 162/172: STIHL, MS 162, 172 Instruction Manual, Canadian edition (0458-200-8221-A, 2025), chapters 3, 5, 23 and 25
Husqvarna 450 II: Husqvarna, Operator's manual 445 II, 445e II, 450 II, 450e II chainsaws (2024-02), safety and technical data
Oregon CS1500: Oregon Tool, Original Instruction Manual, Chainsaw Model CS1500-093 (corded, 230 V), safety and specifications pages
CCOHS chainsaw PPE: CCOHS, Chainsaws - Personal Protective Equipment and Clothing (OSH Answers)
